text:
Mikko Rantanen's week in Vegas is the version of him Dallas paid for: four points on Nov. 17, including the tying goal with five seconds left, then another assist two nights later as the Stars swept the trip. He has 27 points (10 goals) in 22 games, 12 of them on the power play, and our wins-added measure puts him 16th of 552 skaters.

Some of it won't last. He has 10 goals on 6.2 expected goals, shooting 24% after 16% last season, and the Stars have scored 8.6 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His recent shot volume is thin too: 42 shots all season, and two games in his last ten without one.

What's real is the puck carrying. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, and Dallas still controls 54.4% of the 5v5 chances with him out there. Our range has him at 82 to 110 points over a full season, and our numbers see the finishing, not the playmaking, as the part most likely to cool.
